name: Shotgun Smith
caption: Lost a Four Corners elimination bout on the fed's own 29 January 1998 broadcast, then fell short in Manhattan and Big Apple Heavyweight title challenges that spring.

tenures.source: The fed's own 29 January 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"), served in bulleted form. The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: The 911 Kid
caption: Held the BAWF Television Championship into the spring of 1998, retaining it at a house show before losing it to Dial 0 Kid in a title rematch.

tenures.source: The fed's own 29 January 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"), served in bulleted form. The fed's own 31 January 1998 house show in Bridgeport, Connecticut, served in bulleted form. The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Spellbinder
caption: BAWF Manhattan Heavyweight Champion through the spring of 1998, retaining the title in a chaotic finish against Shotgun Smith after a Jason Jinx interference angle.

tenures.source: The fed's own 29 January 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"), served in bulleted form. The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Triad
caption: A Bloodclan enforcer who beat the reigning Television Champion at a January 1998 house show and "Sexy" Rex Harley on Friday Night Heat.

tenures.source: The fed's own 31 January 1998 house show in Bridgeport, Connecticut, served in bulleted form. The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Red Lightning
caption: Won by disqualification over "Dreamlover" Trace Michaels on the fed's own 5 February 1998 Blood & Guts broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts").

name: "Dreamlover" Trace Michaels
caption: Disqualified against Red Lightning after a chair swing on the fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts").

name: "The Warden" Norm Cash
caption: A journeyman who lost by submission to "Sexy" Rex Harley and by pinfall to Junior Steele in successive BAWF broadcasts.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: "Sexy" Rex Harley
caption: Beat "The Warden" Norm Cash by submission before losing to the Bloodclan's Triad in a competitive Friday Night Heat bout.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: "Magnificent" Marcus Mann
caption: Teamed with Leo Cartier in a tag loss to the New Revolution on the fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts").

name: Leo Cartier
caption: Teamed with "Magnificent" Marcus Mann in a tag loss to the New Revolution on the fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts").

name: Ryan Cage
caption: One half of the New Revolution, a tag team that fell just short of the Big Apple Tag Team Championship against the New Generation.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Nick Blade
caption: One half of the New Revolution, a tag team that fell just short of the Big Apple Tag Team Championship against the New Generation.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Brian Steal
caption: Lost by submission to "The Rattlesnake" Butch Mcrae on the fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts").

name: "The Rattlesnake" Butch Mcrae
caption: Beat Brian Steal by submission, then defeated Jon "The King" Levin's opponent slot on a later Friday Night Heat card.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Tyrone Kalm
caption: One half of the New Generation, retaining the Big Apple Tag Team Championship against the New Revolution on Friday Night Heat.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Luke Kalm
caption: One half of the New Generation, retaining the Big Apple Tag Team Championship against the New Revolution on Friday Night Heat.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Ward Enigma
caption: Teamed with The 911 Kid in a disqualification loss to the Schianos on the fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts").

name: Keith Schiano
caption: Won a disqualification tag victory alongside Stonelight, then won a three-way match on Friday Night Heat to earn a Manhattan Heavyweight Championship shot.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts"). The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Stonelight
caption: Teamed with Keith Schiano (his brother Martin, billed under this name) to a disqualification win over The 911 Kid and Ward Enigma.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts").

name: Animosity
caption: Wrestled Shawn Arrows to a thirty-minute time-limit draw on the fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 5 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Blood & Guts").

name: Jon "The King" Levin
caption: Beat "The Rattlesnake" Butch Mcrae with an assist from his manager's crutch on Friday Night Heat.

tenures.source: The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Junior Steele
caption: Beat "The Warden" Norm Cash on Friday Night Heat before losing to Inferno in a Mayday Massacre dark match.

tenures.source: The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat"). The fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast ("Mayday Massacre").

name: Dial 0 Kid
caption: Upset The 911 Kid on Friday Night Heat to become the new BAWF Television Champion.

tenures.source: The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Serpent
caption: Eliminated first from a three-way match on Friday Night Heat that Keith Schiano went on to win.

tenures.source: The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Blazin Skull
caption: Lost to Jimmy "Pretty Boy" Floyd by a small package on Friday Night Heat after a missed top-rope finisher.

tenures.source: The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Rob Atlas
caption: Ended Shawn Arrows's nearly two-month Big Apple Heavyweight Championship reign in a restarted main event on Friday Night Heat.

tenures.source: The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Terry Hardaway
caption: Beat Sensei Slade in a dark match on the fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast ("Mayday Massacre").

name: "Latin King" Miguel Gudino
caption: Fought Jack Cass to a no-contest in a dark match on the fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast ("Mayday Massacre").

name: Jack Cass
caption: Fought Miguel Gudino to a no-contest in a dark match on the fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast ("Mayday Massacre").

name: Inferno
caption: Beat Junior Steele in a dark match on the fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast ("Mayday Massacre").

name: "The Ringmaster" Chris Kill
caption: Ambushed Iceman before the bell on the fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast, then lost by disqualification when a ladder shot backfired.

tenures.source: The fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast ("Mayday Massacre").

name: Iceman
caption: Won by disqualification over "The Ringmaster" Chris Kill on the fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast, accompanied by Brooke.

tenures.source: The fed's own 9 May 1998 joint broadcast ("Mayday Massacre").

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is recorded elsewhere in the held record's other federations; nothing in this wing's own served record links the two.

name: Jason Jinx
caption: A former Manhattan Heavyweight Champion who cost Spellbinder a successful title defense by interfering and then torched the belt on camera, only for the finish to be overturned.

tenures.source: The fed's own 27 February 1998 broadcast ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Aeneas Allen
caption: A rising BAWF star who won by submission (the Allenator) in a preliminary match on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast, then attacked his own beaten opponent afterward.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Sensei Slade
caption: Lost a preliminary match to Aeneas Allen by submission on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Ghetto
caption: One half of the Evil Empire; he and Louie retained the Big Apple Tag Team Championship in a three-way elimination match on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Louie
caption: One half of the Evil Empire; he and Ghetto retained the Big Apple Tag Team Championship in a three-way elimination match on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is recorded elsewhere in the held record's other federations; nothing in this wing's own served record links the two.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Greven
caption: One half of the Fire Brothers, entering the ring from a gold-and-white carriage with his tag partner Rathi Dragon; eliminated first from a three-way tag title match on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Rathi Dragon
caption: One half of the Fire Brothers, a masked luchador-styled wrestler; eliminated with tag partner Greven from a three-way tag title match on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Chris
caption: One half of the Glory Knights, alongside Browen; lost a three-way Big Apple Tag Team Championship match to the Evil Empire on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is recorded elsewhere in the held record's other federations; nothing in this wing's own served record links the two.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Browen
caption: One half of the Glory Knights, alongside Chris; lost a three-way Big Apple Tag Team Championship match to the Evil Empire on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Troy Croft
caption: The reigning BAWF Television Champion, also billed elsewhere in the fed's own record as a former World Heavyweight Champion and a former BAWF Manhattan Champion; he and Lord Wrath won a Dream Partners tag match by count-out on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast, setting up a Television Championship defense against Wrath.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: "The Philosophy Master" Lord Wrath
caption: A masked wrestler managed by Squire Flame; he and Troy Croft won a Dream Partners tag match by count-out on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast, earning a Television Championship shot against Croft.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: "Bullseye" Shawn Arrows
caption: The BAWF Manhattan Heavyweight Champion; on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast his long-estranged father, Clint Arrows, revealed the Big Apple Heavyweight Champion Sephiroth to be his own brother, thought dead since 1992, and Shawn struck him in response.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is recorded elsewhere in the held record's other federations; nothing in this wing's own served record links the two.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: "Offspring" Aaron Oakley
caption: A former BAWF Television Champion who lost a Dream Partners tag match by count-out (alongside Shawn Arrows) on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast, then publicly conceded respect to the reigning champion, Troy Croft.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Sephiroth
caption: The Big Apple Heavyweight Champion, revealed on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast to be Kasey Arrows, the long-lost brother of fellow BAWF wrestler Shawn Arrows, thought dead since 1992; he retained the title that same night in a steel cage match.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is recorded elsewhere in the held record's other federations; nothing in this wing's own served record links the two.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Jimmy "Pretty Boy" Floyd
caption: A former two-time BAWF Television Champion and member of the Powers of Arrogance stable; he challenged for the Big Apple Heavyweight Championship in a steel cage match on the fed's own 24 May 1998 broadcast and lost by pinfall.

tenures.source: The fed's own broadcast posted 24 May 1998 ("BAWF Friday Night Heat").

name: Xylogen
caption: A masked former Missouri Wrestling Alliance wrestler who ambushed a Bloodclan member in disguise before revealing his own BAWF signing, then returned weeks later to wrestle the promotion's own Television Champion.

tenures.source: The fed's own 12 April and 4 May 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcasts.
tenures.note: Introduced as a masked mystery attacker under an MWA t-shirt before unmasking and signing with the fed; a full-length singles match is served on the following month's broadcast.

name: Mike "The Kid" Levin
caption: A newcomer escorted to the ring by his brother, wrestling in the fed's undercard.

tenures.source: The fed's own 4 May 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcast.
tenures.note: Billed from Needham, Massachusetts; escorted by his brother Jon "The King" Levin.

name: Del Danson
caption: A brash rookie who cut a promo challenging Lord Wrath before wrestling his first televised match a month later against a fellow BAWF Training Camp graduate.

tenures.source: The fed's own 12 April and 18 May 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcasts.
tenures.note: Introduced as a new signing on 12 April with a public challenge to Lord Wrath; wrestles his own debut match on 18 May.

name: Dark Shadow
caption: The BAWF Training Camp's first graduate, debuting in a hard-fought win over a fellow newcomer.

tenures.source: The fed's own 18 May 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcast.
tenures.note: Billed as the BAWF Training Camp's first graduate.

name: "Pink" Floyd
caption: A talked-up newcomer who lost a hard-fought singles debut on the outside brawling style of a tag-team convert.

identity.note: Shares a surname only with the established BAWF heel Jimmy "Pretty Boy" Floyd, billed separately by first name and hometown on the same broadcast; no relationship is stated in the record.

tenures.source: The fed's own 18 May 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcast.
tenures.note: Billed as a newcomer; lost to "Raw Dawg" Tyrone Kalm by submission.

name: Jack Vars
caption: A recurring ally of "The Ringmaster" Chris Kill, wrestling BAWF's first-ever Table Break Match.

identity.note: A bare name shared with several other 1998-era e-fed rosters; no operator, roster, or storyline overlap found with any of them, so no join is asserted.

tenures.source: The fed's own 18 May 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcast; earlier interference appearances on the 12 April and 4 May broadcasts.
tenures.note: Lost a Table Break Match to "Offspring" Aaron Oakley.

name: "VIP" Eddie Zam
caption: One half of a title-holding tag team who joined a growing faction with the fed's own top singles stars.

identity.note: The RSPWF Top 200 poll's own "VIP" Eddie Zam (1998, tagged MWA) is this character: the fed's own 12 April 1998 broadcast narrates the VIP Treatment gimmick as already known at MWA events, a sibling NWC region.

tenures.source: The fed's own 12 April and 18 May 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcasts.

notes: Came in at #169 in the RSPWF Top 200 for 1998, tagged MWA, under this same billing.

name: Big Hurt
caption: The other half of a title-holding tag team who joined a growing faction with the fed's own top singles stars.

tenures.source: The fed's own 12 April 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcast.

name: Iceberg
caption: An Icelandic wrestler who scored a first-round upset in the fed's own Manhattan Heavyweight Title tournament.

tenures.source: The fed's own 16 April 1998 "New York Live" newsmagazine segment.
tenures.note: Billed from Iceland with tag partner The Killer Rock.

name: "GT" Chris Austin
caption: A young wrestler pinned inside a handicap match marking Sephiroth's own return from injury.

tenures.source: The fed's own 6 March 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcast.
tenures.note: Teamed with "The Rattlesnake" Butch McRae in a handicap match.

name: BadAss Blood
caption: A low-seeded tournament entrant whose kickouts nearly upset a returning former challenger.

tenures.source: The fed's own 12 April 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcast.
tenures.note: Billed the #32 seed of the Manhattan Heavyweight Title tournament, entering the match 0-15.

name: Doomstar
caption: A small BAWF Training Camp-adjacent wrestler who lost a first-round tournament match by submission.

tenures.source: The fed's own 12 April 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcast.
tenures.note: Billed from Greensborough, North Carolina, the #23 seed of the Manhattan Heavyweight Title tournament.

name: The Aggressive Warrior
caption: A former member of Lord Wrath's own stable, released for losing too often, who nearly upset his old ally in a tournament match.

tenures.source: The fed's own 12 April 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcast.
tenures.note: Billed as a former member of Lord Wrath's own Brothers of Fire, released from the group for losing.

name: "Mean" Mark Green
caption: A Bloodclan member who advanced in the Manhattan Heavyweight Title tournament off a disqualification finish.

identity.note: Shares a name only with the BAWF commissioner character "Magic" Mark Greene, who is spelled and billed differently and appears separately on the same broadcasts as an authority figure, never as a wrestler.

tenures.source: The fed's own 12 April 1998 Friday Night Heat broadcast.
tenures.note: A member of the Bloodclan stable.
